# Points system

How progress points are earned, capped, and turned into levels and steps. Everything here is read from the shipped code and migrations; each section names the file that owns the number.

Last checked against the code: 2026-10-08 (review points are a flat 0.25; badge tiers pay rewards).

## The short version

| Action | Points |
| --- | --- |
| Complete (publish) a pattern | **10.0** |
| Review a contact's post (any verdict) | **0.25 flat, once per post** |
| Add a medal to a supporting review | **0.0** (medals count toward badges, not points) |
| Complete a badge to-do list item | **0.0** |
| Complete a badge tier (Bronze/Silver/Gold) | **10 / 30 / 60 / 100 / 180** for a badge of level 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5, once per tier |
| Complete a whole badge | **nothing beyond its tier rewards** |
| Daily ceiling for completions and reviews | **30.0 per local day** (badge-tier rewards are outside it) |
| Whole path | **12,000 points, 5 levels, 7 steps each** |

Badges stay optional: they never gate levels or later badges. Since 2026-09-15 each completed tier pays a one-time reward. See [Badge tier rewards](#badge-tier-rewards) and `BADGE_POINT_REWARDS.md`.

## Where points come from

There are three award paths in the app, all in `CompletionPointsService`:

- [CompletionPointsService.swift:237](../../../Paths/Services/CompletionPointsService.swift#L237) — `awardCompletionPoints`, called from [SupabaseUserPatternsStore.swift:719](../../../Paths/Storage/Supabase/SupabaseUserPatternsStore.swift#L719)
- [CompletionPointsService.swift:266](../../../Paths/Services/CompletionPointsService.swift#L266) — `awardFeedbackPoints`, called from [PatternReviewSheet.swift:250](../../../Paths/Views/CoreViews/Social/PatternReviewSheet.swift#L250)
- [CompletionPointsService.swift:200](../../../Paths/Services/CompletionPointsService.swift#L200) — `syncBadgeRewards`, called after checklist writes ([SupabaseProgressStore.swift:410](../../../Paths/Storage/Supabase/SupabaseProgressStore.swift#L410), [:519](../../../Paths/Storage/Supabase/SupabaseProgressStore.swift#L519)) and by the badge checkpoint ([BadgeRequirementSyncService.swift:366](../../../Paths/Services/BadgeRequirementSyncService.swift#L366))

No other surface can mint points. For completions and reviews the client only ever *requests* an amount; the server settles it in `award_progress_points_secure` ([20260823182418_progress_point_awards_fix_param_shadowing.sql](../../../supabase/migrations/20260823182418_progress_point_awards_fix_param_shadowing.sql)). For badge tiers the client sends only its local day; `award_badge_tier_points_secure` ([20260915230000_badge_tier_point_rewards.sql](../../../supabase/migrations/20260915230000_badge_tier_point_rewards.sql)) decides which tiers pay and how much.

### 1. Completing a pattern — 10.0 points

`Levels.baseCompletionPoints = 10.0` ([Levels.swift:331](../../../Paths/Models/Progress/Levels.swift#L331)).

The award fires from the write path that records the completion, not from a view, so a completion published from the phone, the watch, or any other surface earns the same 10 points. It is only paid when the stored row transitions from not-completed to completed (`patternInstance.didIt && !wasCompleted`), so republishing or editing the same completion pays nothing extra.

The award key is `pattern_completion:<pattern_id>:<instance_id>:<ddMMyyyy>` ([CompletionPointsService.swift:185](../../../Paths/Services/CompletionPointsService.swift#L185)). Consequences of that key:

- The same pattern instance completed on a **different day** is a new earning event and earns again.
- A **different instance** of the same pattern on the same day is its own earning event.
- A retry of the same completion collides on the key and is a no-op, across devices.

With the daily cap of 30, **3 pattern completions per local day** is the maximum that pays. A fourth completion the same day is recorded but credits 0 (`ProgressPointsAwardTests.testTheDailyCapIsThreeBaseCompletions`).

### 2. Reviewing a post — a flat 0.25

A review ([PatternReview.swift](../../../Paths/Models/Patterns/PatternReview.swift), sheet in [PatternReviewSheet.swift](../../../Paths/Views/CoreViews/Social/PatternReviewSheet.swift)) asks one question, whether the evidence supports completing the pattern, with three verdicts: Supports completion, Needs more evidence, Does not support completion. An explanation is required unless the verdict supports completion. Every saved review requests a flat **0.25** points whatever the verdict ([PatternReviewSheet.swift:250](../../../Paths/Views/CoreViews/Social/PatternReviewSheet.swift#L250)), so a critical review pays exactly as much as a supportive one.

A bronze, silver or gold medal can be added only to a supporting review. It pays no points; it counts toward the "Give N posts any medal" badge requirements.

The award key is `feedback_given:<target_pattern_id>:<target_instance_id>:<target_date_key>` — keyed by the post being answered, so revising a review on the same post never pays twice.

The aspect-based feedback this section used to describe (0.25 per positive aspect, plus 1 / 2 / 3 points per medal) is retired; the app no longer offers it.

## Badge tier rewards

Badges are an optional accomplishment track. They never gate levels or later badges; the product rule is stated at the top of [BadgeTierCatalog.swift](../../../Paths/Models/Progress/BadgeTierCatalog.swift). Since 2026-09-15 each independently completed tier pays a one-time reward ([BADGE_POINT_REWARDS.md](BADGE_POINT_REWARDS.md)):

- `BadgeProgression.bonusPoints(level:badgeNumber:)` returns 10, 30, 60, 100 or 180 for a badge of level 1 to 5 ([Levels.swift:142-146](../../../Paths/Models/Progress/Levels.swift#L142-L146)); the badge plan's label reads "+N points per tier" ([Levels.swift:56-58](../../../Paths/Models/Progress/Levels.swift#L56-L58)). `badgeBonusPercents` stays `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`: there is no percentage bonus ([Levels.swift:74](../../../Paths/Models/Progress/Levels.swift#L74)).
- The server decides. `award_badge_tier_points_secure` pays each tier whose requirement keys are all completed in `user_badge_requirements`, for badges at or below the user's level, once per tier (`badge_tier_completed:<level>:<badge>:<tier>`). A later-level user completing an earlier badge gets that badge's original amount.
- The rewards are outside the 30-point daily cap and inside the 12,000-point path cap; the last one can be partial or zero.
- Ticking a single to-do item earns nothing; only closing a whole tier pays. Tiers are independent, so a Gold tier does not imply Bronze or Silver.

What a to-do item *can* also do is describe an action that separately earns points. For example, the Study I Bronze item "Complete any pattern 3 times" pays nothing as a checklist item, but those three completions pay 10 each through the completion award — that is 30, which is also the whole daily cap if they happen on one day — and closing the tier adds its 10-point reward on top.

There are 15 badges (5 levels × 3) and 45 tiers (15 × 3) in the catalog, nine rewards per level: 90 + 270 + 540 + 900 + 1,620 = **3,420 points** from all of them.

## Caps

### Daily cap: 30.0 points per local day

`Levels.dailyProgressPointCap = 30.0` on the client, and `daily_cap constant numeric := 30` in the RPC. The server is authoritative; the client constant exists only so the UI does not promise a payment that will not land. The cap covers completions and reviews; badge-tier rewards bypass it.

The cap is a **local-day** rule. The client sends its own `ddMMyyyy` day key from the device time zone, and the server bounds it to within one day of UTC today so a fabricated key cannot mint fresh allowances.

Partial payment happens: if 28 points are already earned today and a completion requests 10, exactly 2.0 are credited. The award row is still written with `points_awarded = 0` or the partial amount, so the same event can never be retried later into a full payment.

### Path cap: 12,000 points

`total_path_points()` sums the `levels` table, which totals 12,000. Once the stored total reaches it, further awards credit 0. Level is clamped to 5 beyond that point.

## Levels

Five levels, seeded identically in Swift ([Levels.swift:337](../../../Paths/Models/Progress/Levels.swift#L337)) and in SQL ([20260627090000_five_level_badge_ladder.sql](../../../supabase/migrations/20260627090000_five_level_badge_ladder.sql)).

| Level | Points to complete the level | Cumulative total at level end | Level spans totals | Days at the 30/day cap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 300 | 300 | 0 – 299 | 10 |
| 2 | 900 | 1,200 | 300 – 1,199 | 30 |
| 3 | 1,800 | 3,000 | 1,200 – 2,999 | 60 |
| 4 | 3,200 | 6,200 | 3,000 – 6,199 | 106.7 |
| 5 | 5,800 | 12,000 | 6,200 – 12,000 | 193.3 |
| **All** | **12,000** | — | — | **400** |

From completions and reviews alone, at the daily cap, the whole path takes a minimum of 400 days; badge-tier rewards (up to 3,420 points, outside the cap) can shorten that. In pattern completions alone, the path is 1,200 completions (12,000 ÷ 10).

The level a total falls in is computed the same way in both places — consume each level's total in order, and a remainder that no longer fits moves up a level. `Levels.calculateLevelAndStep` and `public.level_for_total_points` must agree, or level-up notifications fire on the wrong completion; that parity is pinned by `ProgressPointsAwardTests.testLevelBoundariesAgreeWithTheServerLadder`.

## Steps within a level

Every level has exactly 7 steps. Steps 3, 5 and 7 are "heavy" and cost 2.5× a "light" step, so a level is `4 light + 3 heavy = 11.5 × light`. That is why each level's light value is its total ÷ 11.5.

| Level | Light step (1, 2, 4, 6) | Heavy step (3, 5, 7) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 26.09 | 65.22 |
| 2 | 78.26 | 195.65 |
| 3 | 156.52 | 391.30 |
| 4 | 278.26 | 695.65 |
| 5 | 504.35 | 1,260.87 |

Step counts are derived from the stored total on read; `current_step` is deliberately not written server-side so the heavy/light economy has only one home.

## Worked examples

**A typical active day.** Two completions (20) plus reviews of three posts (3 × 0.25 = 0.75) = 20.75 points; 9.25 more fit before the cap.

**A heavy day.** Four completions and six reviews request 41.5; exactly 30.0 is credited and the rest is recorded as capped-out award rows. Nothing carries over to tomorrow.

**A first week at the cap.** 7 × 30 = 210 points, which lands mid-level 1 between step 5 (208.70) and step 6 (234.78). Level 1 closes on day 10.

**A badge-focused day.** Closing Pillar I Bronze — submit the Brief and fill in the "Who am I?" questionnaire — earns that tier's 10-point reward on the next badge sync, on top of whatever the day's completions and reviews earned.
